tasks.prompt: A teammate asks you to promote one especially promising candidate test directly into the blocking lane outside the scheduled batch process because it improves a dashboard metric. Decide how to respond under this skill's rules, including whether ad-hoc promotion is allowed and whether metric pressure changes the answer.

You run the full promotion pipeline and every candidate is eliminated by eligibility checks, change-detector screening, mutant-utility dedup, or kata failure. Decide what the correct outcome is and whether you should still try to promote something to avoid an empty report or keep metrics healthy.

A service has more invariant candidates in the queue than the weekly ratification budget allows. Decide which candidates should reach the human this week by applying the queue policy: incident-derived candidates first, then candidates covering uncovered capabilities, while overflow expires back to the queue. Explain the ranking and which items must wait or expire.

A promotion batch has survivors, but the draft PR only lists the test names and omits the screening evidence table. Decide whether the batch is acceptable to send for approval as-is, and explain what must be included to satisfy the anti-laundering guardrail.

After a batch screen, several candidate tests look obviously safe, and someone suggests landing them straight into the blocking lane without opening a PR to save time. Decide whether this is permitted and state the required path for any change that touches the blocking lane or ratified verification artifacts.

Review several invariant candidates waiting in the ratification queue. For each one, decide whether it should proceed, be sent back to the author, be rejected for contract contradiction, or be merged/dropped as a duplicate. Use the mechanical pre-filter rules: each package needs both passing runs and a concrete violating trace, contradictions against declared capability contracts cannot be passed through silently, and duplicates or implications versus the ratified set should not consume reviewer time.

A scheduled promotion batch is due for the candidate lane. Evaluate a set of candidate tests and decide which ones, if any, survive the batch promotion pipeline: only include tests still within TTL, with at least the minimum advisory runs, stable records, and no pinning; reject any change detector caught by a behavior-preserving refactor commit; discard any test that adds no new mutant kills beyond the blocking lane; and require the candidate suite to fail every known-bad kata for its capability. Explain which tests should be rejected, discarded, or advanced to the human-review sample, and note that an empty batch is acceptable.

You are preparing a promotion batch, but the refactor corpus has fewer than five commits and one capability represented in the candidate suite has no kata coverage. Decide whether to proceed, skip only the missing checks, or bail. Provide the correct decision and name the prerequisite gaps that must be fixed before screening can continue.
